sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Accession**: Born as Nizam Khan, he succeeded his father Bahlul Lodhi in 1489, overcoming challenges from his brother Barbak Shah.
• **Administrative Centralization**: Unlike the tribal confederacy model of Bahlul, Sikander asserted the **divine right of kingship** and enforced strict discipline among Afghan nobles.
• **Economic Reform**: Introduced the **Gaj-i-Sikandari** (30 digits or 32 inches), a standardized unit of measurement for land revenue assessment.
• **Urban Development**: Founded **Agra** in 1504 to strategically control the rebellious regions of Doab and Bayana.

The pen name under which Sikander Lodhi composed Persian poetry; reflects the cultural synthesis of the era.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Land Revenue**: Systematic measurement of land (Paimaish) to ensure accurate tax collection.
• **Trade & Commerce**: Abolition of internal duties (Zakat) on grain to stabilize food prices.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Constant friction with Afghan nobles who resented his autocratic style.
• **Solutions**: Use of a robust intelligence network to monitor noble activities.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'A-G-A-P' (Agra, Gaj-i-Sikandari, Afghan control, Poetry/Gulrukhi).
• **Decoded Meaning**: A (Agra founded 1504), G (Gaj-i-Sikandari measurement), A (Afghan nobility control), P (Poetry under pen name Gulrukhi).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Gaj-i-Sikandari' with the 'Dahsala' system. Remember: Gaj-i-Sikandari is a measurement unit (Lodhi), while Dahsala is a revenue system (Akbar).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Sultanate Centralization' to describe his reign, contrasting it with the 'Tribal Confederation' of Bahlul Lodhi.

keyTakeaways: Sikander Lodhi was the most powerful ruler of the Lodhi dynasty, shifting the power center to Agra.
His administrative legacy, specifically the Gaj-i-Sikandari, influenced revenue systems for over a century.
His reign marked a transition from the loose Afghan tribal structure to a more centralized, autocratic Sultanate.
